components.notes: Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.989(a), "Sworn Statement in Support of Petition", printed caption SWORN STATEMENT. This is the same instrument the component always named; only its title changed, on 2019-12-19, when the Supreme Court of Florida struck AFFIDAVIT and inserted SWORN STATEMENT in the rule heading, the subdivision heading, the form's printed caption and the first numbered averment. Sworn to and subscribed before a notary public or other person authorized to administer an oath. The rule's own words are "NOTARY PUBLIC, or other person authorized to administer an oath"; it does not say deputy clerk, though a deputy clerk is such an authorized person under Florida law. It is mandatory and the requirement value must not be relaxed: § 943.059(3)(b), Fla. Stat. makes the petition complete only when accompanied by the petitioner's sworn statement, and a knowingly false sworn statement is a third-degree felony. There is no standalone official PDF of this instrument and there never has been. The Supreme Court of Florida publishes it as rule text inside the rule itself, so the authority is the rule and there is nothing to acquire from an issuer. No form number is created here and no standalone PDF identity is created for rule text.

_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.defectOnThisTrack: Stale title on the right instrument. Same defect and same remedy as fl-expunction: the component named the pre-2019 Affidavit title of Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.989(a) and now names the current Sworn Statement title of the same subdivision.
_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.amendingInstrument: In re: Amendments to Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure 3.692 and 3.989 — 2019 Fast-Track Report, SC19-1983, 286 So. 3d 214 (Fla. 2019), decided 2019-12-19. The redline struck AFFIDAVIT and inserted SWORN STATEMENT in four places within the one instrument and propagated the rename into Rule 3.692, so the retitle was systematic rather than cosmetic. The same opinion adopted Rule 3.9895 and moved the human-trafficking subdivisions into it.
_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.noLaterAmendment: None. The official compilation's Effective Date / Citation / Description table was read to its final row and no row after 12-19-19 references Rule 3.989, and the rule's own Committee Notes end with the 2019 amendment note recording that the human-trafficking subdivisions moved to Rule 3.9895.
rule3989SubdivisionsToday: (a) Sworn Statement in Support of Petition
rule39895SubdivisionsToday: (a) Petition to Expunge; Human Trafficking Victim
(b) Sworn Statement in Support of Petition; Human Trafficking Victim
(c) Order to Expunge; Human Trafficking Victim
_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.publicationForm: There is no standalone official PDF of this instrument and there never has been. The Supreme Court of Florida publishes it as rule text inside the rule itself, so the authority is the rule and there is nothing to acquire from an issuer. No form number is created here and no standalone PDF identity is created for rule text.
whatWasNotDone: No form number was invented and no standalone PDF identity was created for rule text. The identity strings name rule subdivisions, which is what the instruments are.
No second component was created for either instrument. Three components were rebound in place; the component count on every Florida track is unchanged.

The retired continuation identity was not reopened. It was resolved in a prior job as naming no document and remains retired, and its literal is deliberately not reproduced here so that no string survives in this memo for a component binding, a relationship row or an acceptance check to match on.

The merged repeatable additional-arrest order-data requirement on the Rule 3.989(b) proposed-order component is untouched, as is the conditional additionalDirectlyRelatedArrests participant input that feeds it.

FDLE Form 40-021 is untouched and remains a separate pre-court agency application bound at its own primary_filing component. It carries its own sworn averments, which makes it superficially similar to the court's sworn statement; it is not a substitute for it.
No output strategy was changed. The three components remain official_pdf_fill, as do the petition and order components alongside them.
No unrelated Florida route was touched and no track, node or component count changed.
documentsExpresslyNotSubstituted: Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.989(d), Petition to Expunge or Seal — the petition, not the sworn statement. Both live in the same rule and both are participant-signed, so a reader matching on rule number alone can bind the wrong subdivision.
Rule 3.989(a) on the trafficking route, and Rule 3.9895(b) on the general routes. Two near-identical instruments implementing different statutes; conflating them is exactly the defect corrected here.
FDLE Form 40-021, Application for a Certificate of Eligibility — an agency application filed with the Department before any court filing.

Circuit and county clerk expunction packets, including the retained Duval and St Johns assets. Local reproductions across 20 circuits and 67 counties; none is the Supreme Court's instrument and none may be promoted to statewide scope.
Commercial rule republications, several of which still carry the pre-2019 title and are a plausible origin of the affidavit framing in the corpus.
The 2017 compilation still served at HTTP 200 on an official host, which carries the superseded title and is six years stale.
The 1984 Adoption Committee Note inside the current rule, which contains the only occurrence of the word affidavit anywhere in the rule. It is a historical note, not operative text.
_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.scope: Statewide prescription with circuit-court venue. The instruments are prescribed statewide by the Supreme Court of Florida and apply in every circuit; the form itself is captioned for a circuit-court filing. The track geography records the venue, not a limit on the form's authority, and statewide prescription does not license substituting a circuit or county packet reproduction.
_swornStatementIdentityCorrection.acquisitionEffect: None required. No issuer interaction can produce a standalone binary that has never been published, so the open download expectation against this identity is a phantom and should not remain an open acquisition job. Nothing was acquired, materialized, digested or receipted by this correction.
openItemsHandedOff: The rest of the fl-trafficking track needs the same 2019 review. Its primary_filing and proposed_order components still name Rule 3.989 identities while the track's basis is § 943.0583, which suggests the same carve-out was missed across the track; Rule 3.9895(a) and (c) are the corresponding trafficking petition and order. Establishing those two identities was outside the integrated decision, which covered the sworn statement only, and is outside this correction. Owner: the Florida legal-design owner.

One repository identity previously served two different rules. The edition amendment should split the human-trafficking usage to its own Rule 3.9895(b) identity, which this correction now reflects in the memo. Owner: the edition publication job.

Whether official_pdf_fill remains the right output strategy for instruments the courts publish only as rule text is a live question for the Florida family, and it reaches the petition and order components as well as these three. It was not answered here because it is not this job's question and changing it would move the source denominator. Owner: the Florida legal-design owner.
Local packet variation across 20 circuits and 67 counties remains recorded as a release blocker on the affected tracks and is untouched.

determinations.text: The Rule 3.989 sworn statement, petition and order are COMPOSE_FROM_AUTHORITY. The applicable FDLE application or certificate attaches as a SEPARATE official component: the sealing component for sealing and the expunction component for expunction. Do not retain one ambiguous certificate component.

determinations.stillOwed: The FDLE split. Every Florida family currently naming one FDLE-CERTIFICATE-OF-ELIGIBILITY-APPLICATION must name the sealing or the expunction component by route. That is a source-identity change, not a composition question, and it is NOT satisfied by this determination alone.
determinations.whatIsComposedAndWhatIsNot: Only the statutory or rule instrument itself is composed from codified text. Every other named form remains an official document that must be held, indexed and hash-matched like any other — listed per family as remainOfficialAndMustBeHeld.
